results.summary: The outlet-dam crossing pin sat on the small saddle dam on the lake's west side, so it moves to the real outlet dam at the lake's north end; the lake pin, which sits mid-lake, is renamed from 'east shore' to plain 'Colchuck Lake'.
results.evidence: Pin 2 'Outlet dam creek crossing' (47.4948,-120.8362) matches the dam inventory's Colchuck Lake SADDLE dam (47.49476,-120.83613, west side of the lake), not the outlet. The main Colchuck Lake Dam is listed at 47.49826,-120.83274, and OpenStreetMap starts the outlet stream at 47.49839,-120.83256 with the mapped 'Balanced Rock climber's access trail' beginning beside it at 47.49837,-120.83246 — agreement within ~25 m, and it matches the route text (small dam at the north end, cross the outlet, continue on the far side). Moved to 47.49832,-120.83265; ground 5560 ft. Pin 1 (47.4919578,-120.8335801) is the lake centroid used by ~20 other routes (OSM lake centre 47.49314,-120.83325, ~130 m) and sits in the water, so it cannot be an 'east shore'; renamed rather than moved, since no source places the point the text means. Pins 0 (trailhead, within ~30 m of OSM's Stuart Lake Trailhead), 3 (rock step, ~70 m off the mapped climbers' trail), 4 (boulder camp) and 5 (col) have no published coordinates to check against and are left; note pin 3 stores 6000 ft where the ground reads ~6680 ft and pin 4 stores 7400 ft where the ground reads ~7800 ft — heights not changed because the pins are not moved. The finding about dist_km is not a pin issue and is not addressed here.

results.summary: The Crystal Creek turnoff pin sat high on the ridge north of Ingalls Creek and the Crystal Lake pin sat east of McClellan Peak; both move to where the trail meets Crystal Creek and to the lake itself, west of the peak.
results.evidence: Pin 1 'Crystal Creek Junction' (47.472,-120.755) reads ~6,710 ft on the ground, far above the valley trail, and is ~5 km east of Crystal Creek. The USGS names record (GNIS 1518369) puts the mouth of Crystal Creek at 47.44790,-120.81482; OpenStreetMap has the Ingalls Creek Trail fording Crystal Creek at 47.44764,-120.81391 (~75 m apart). Moved to 47.44768,-120.81400 on the trail at the crossing; ground 3,780 ft. Pin 2 'Crystal Lake' (47.471,-120.78) sits on the slope east of McClellan Peak (ground ~7,350 ft). OpenStreetMap places Crystal Lake at 47.47434,-120.80271 and the USGS names record starts Crystal Creek (the lake's outlet) at 47.47362,-120.80001 (~220 m); a published trip report gives the lake as 7,000 ft and the ground at the new point reads 7,030 ft. Pin 3 'Crystal Lake Tower' (47.47,-120.792) is ~290 m from the climbing database's tower coordinate (47.46872,-120.79532) and ~500 m west of the USGS McClellan Peak summit (47.46994,-120.78566), consistent with the west end of the summit ridge; left (one source). Pin 0 trailhead is within ~20 m of OpenStreetMap's Ingalls Creek Trailhead; left. distMi values unchanged (no source gives them). The drawn line is a 4-point sketch through the old pins and will no longer pass through the two moved pins.

results.summary: The Bird Creek Camp pin sat on the summit of Tupshin Peak, over 8,000 ft; it moves down to the camp's real spot on the Devore Creek Trail just short of the Bird Creek crossing, at about 4,200 ft.
results.evidence: Pin 2 'Bird Creek Camp' (48.296118718181816,-120.75108514545455) is ~60 m from the USGS names record's Tupshin Peak summit (48.29691,-120.75072) and reads ~8,120 ft on the ground, so it was taken from the neighbouring peak. The route text puts the camp about four miles up the Devore Creek Trail from Weaver Point, about 100 ft before the trail crosses Bird Creek, at ~4,200 ft. OpenStreetMap has the Devore Creek Trail fording Bird Creek at 48.28073,-120.73059, and the USGS names record puts the mouth of Bird Creek (where it meets Devore Creek, beside the trail) at 48.28042,-120.72873 (~145 m apart). Moved to 48.28090,-120.73030 on the trail just before the ford; ground 4,170 ft, matching the stated 4,200 ft. Summit pin 6 matches the USGS Devore Peak coordinate exactly; pin 0 agrees with a neighbouring route's Harlequin pin within ~20 m; pin 1 sits on the Stehekin River side about half a mile west of the USGS Weaver Point, as the text says (its stored 1,500 ft is ~330 ft above the ground reading, not changed because the pin is not moved). Pin 3 (upper basin, ~7,030 ft ground) sits near the head of Bird Creek as the text describes. Pin 4 'Saddle west of Point 7657' sits only ~90 m from pin 3 in the basin (ground ~7,040 ft, not the ~7,500 ft col on the southeast ridge), but no source gives the saddle's position closely enough to move it; left and flagged. Pin 5 left. A different route (Tupshin Peak scramble) pins its own Bird Creek Camp ~3 km north on Devore Creek; not in this file.

results.summary: The Lichtenberg Boulders pin belongs to the west-side approach from the Valhalla trail, which this route never uses, so it is removed; the remaining pins are right.
results.evidence: This route goes from the first switchback of Smith Brook Road to Lichtenwasser Lake, then climbs southwest to the 5,640 ft saddle on the southeast ridge and follows the ridge to the summit; nothing in its approach, beta or itinerary visits the boulder field. Pin 2 'Lichtenberg Boulders' carries distMi 2.5, the mileage of the Valhalla-trail approach, and the identical pin appears on the west-side route (wa_lichtenberg_mountain_west_face_west_rib), where it belongs. Removed; the route keeps its trailhead and summit. Checked the rest: pin 1 matches OpenStreetMap's Lichtenwasser Lake (47.79244,-121.07682) within ~10 m and the stated 4,708 ft; pin 0 reads 3,980 ft on the ground, matching the text's first hairpin near 3,970 ft; the summit pin reads 5,844 ft on the ground, its stated height.
